## Context
Owner report 2026-11-27: on another Windows machine, terminal update and a fresh install hang 553 s in "WSL tools: check 17 release tools", then fail with a KeyboardInterrupt in the TLS handshake of WSL python to GitHub. Cause in code: the parallel prefetch gives each repo a 60 s socket timeout; when it fails, run() and check() call latest_tag again one tool at a time (60 s each), and release_of/fetch use 120 s. So a filtered network costs about 17 x 60 s sequentially. Why the handshake stalls on that machine is unknown.

Finding (from code, not measured): release_install.prefetched() runs latest_tag for all repos in parallel, each with a 60 s socket timeout. When a lookup fails, run() and check() call latest_tag again, one tool at a time, each with up to 60 s per blocking step (connect, then TLS). fetch() uses 120 s. [plan, basicly-meta, 2026-11-27 11:20 UTC] One-page plan, part 1 of 2: "everything is a plugin" for the meta harness (Orchestrator order 11:11 UTC).

1. MEANING FOR BASICLY
- deepseek-harness (README.md:7, AGENTS.md:3) makes every part, core included, a Cordis plugin mounted at run time.
- basicly refused that absolute form: D-43 P4 ("no privileged core") and P2 (a runtime mounted from configuration), docs/architecture/architecture.md section D-43; review row A1, docs/research/deepseek-harness-plugin-review.md (basicly-gtb19bg.28).
- Inside that line, "plugin" means two things only:
  (a) Meta harness side: each coding agent is an adapter plugin in the entry point group basicly_orch.adapters (built in v0, basicly-e44r45l). An adapter declares what it can do, and orch delegate reads only those declarations (T3 Y1, deepseek B3).
  (b) Catalog side: a repository installs a named profile of basicly capabilities. That is basicly-gtb19bg.29 and its open children .29.2, .29.3, .29.5 to .29.8. They stay there; I file nothing twice under qpr2xmr.4.
- Anything beyond (a) and (b), for example plugin sessions, hot reload or a plugin event bus, is refused unless a new decision reopens D-43.

2. EFFECT ON THE qpr2xmr.4 CHILDREN
- 4.1 repository as consumer: NEEDS DECISION (decision 2). v0 lives in the basicly-orch kit (owner 2026-11-26, comment on 4.1). basicly-lddx5vr, which 4.1 was to double as, is closed. docs/research/meta-harness.md line 39 still says 4.2 to 4.6 move to the new repository.
- 4.2 v1 one Claude session: framing changes, acceptance unchanged. The session host becomes the claude adapter plus capability flags. Its text needs bubblewrap and stream-json, and the v1 plan comment of 2026-11-26 defers bubblewrap until the R11 measurement. Blocked by 4.1 and qpr2xmr.1.
- 4.3 Copilot over ACP and 4.4 Codex over app-server: framing changes. Each becomes a transport capability of an existing adapter, with the same contract test. Both texts need ACP or app-server, which the v1 plan defers (decision 3). 4.4 also waits on qpr2xmr.2 (vendor permission).
- 4.5 workflows: unchanged in scope. A workflow step names a capability, and a missing one is refused by name before the step starts. This depends on the first cut.
- 4.6 handily views: unchanged.
- qpr2xmr.6 (requirements text for capability flags) and qpr2xmr.7 (outcome vocabulary): unchanged. The first cut gives .6 running code to cite. The cut leaves out .7 and the permission ceiling (Y3).

[plan part 2 of 2, basicly-meta, 2026-11-27]
3. FIRST CUT, about one day, in the basicly-orch kit (.basicly/core/kit/orch/orch_relay)
New child record under basicly-qpr2xmr.4: "Adapters declare their capabilities, and orch delegate checks a plugin when it loads".
Measured today (code read on main a70583e5):
- adapters.py _plugins() calls point.load() with no guard, and registry() runs it on every adapter() call. So one broken plugin also stops orch delegate --vendor claude.
- Capabilities are loose attributes. names_session is read directly (delegate.py:115), so a plugin without it fails with AttributeError. resumes_read_only is read with getattr default False (delegate.py:170, 178).
- No command lists the adapters and where each comes from.
Acceptance criteria:
- AC1: When a plugin's entry point fails to load or lacks a required method or capability, then orch delegate refuses only that plugin by its entry point name, and the built-in adapters still run. Test: new test in tests/test_orch_delegate.py, next to test_an_installed_plugin_adds_a_coding_agent.
- AC2: When an adapter is registered, then it declares one capabilities value (names_session, resumes_read_only, read_only, lane_edits), and delegate.py reads only that value, with no getattr default. Test: extend the read-only resume tests in tests/test_orch_delegate.py.
- AC3: When a turn asks for a capability its adapter does not declare, then orch delegate refuses before any process starts and names the adapter and the capability. Test: the Codex read-only resume refusal comes from this rule.
- AC4: When orch delegate --list runs, then it prints each adapter with its origin (built-in, or the distribution of the entry point) and its capabilities. Test: one new test in tests/test_orch_delegate.py.
- Docs: packages/basicly-orch/README.md, section "Coding agents", plus changelog.d/<record>.added.md.
- Consumer with no engine: the capability ships in the orch kit under .basicly/core/kit/orch, installed by basicly install or the basicly-orch package. It needs no src/basicly import.
- No dependency, workflow or ignore-file edit. No new GitHub repository.
- Proof: uv run pytest tests/test_orch_delegate.py -q locally, then the PR CI run id with queue and run time. No full suite.
Risks:
- tests/test_orch_delegate.py is 12,154 bytes against the module-size cap of 4,000 tokens (read_cost.py:64). If it passes the cap, the new tests go to a sibling file, and the commit body says why. A new file can also trip the lane ceiling of test_decompose.
- A plugin package outside this repository that has no capabilities value would be refused after this change. None is known, by search for basicly_orch.adapters in this workspace.
- Scope creep into Y3 (permission ceiling) or qpr2xmr.7. I file those as follow-ups instead.

[requirements: dispatch outcome vocabulary, basicly-qpr2xmr.7, basicly-meta 2026-11-27; decided by the orchestrator on basicly-qpr2xmr.4]
Source: docs/research/deepseek-harness-plugin-review.md, concepts B1 (a dispatch result that never rejects and carries a stop reason) and B17 (a code discriminator on the single blocked state).
D1. A dispatch result never rejects. Every orch delegate run ends with one result: an outcome, a cause and an exit code. No error passes orch delegate as a crash or as bare prose. Its last line is "outcome: OUTCOME cause: CAUSE".
D2. The outcomes, with their exit codes:
- answered (0): the agent gave an answer, and it is written on the record. Cause: none.
- usage_limit (3): the agent refused the turn at its usage limit. Cause: reset_known or reset_unknown.
- refused (1): orch delegate refused before any coding agent started. Nothing ran and nothing was written.
- failed (4): a process started, but no answer came back. The failure is saved under delegations/failures.
D3. Refusal causes, each named by the check that refused: unknown_agent, plugin_refused (a plugin that fails to load or lacks a method or capability), capability (the turn needs a capability that the adapter does not declare), bad_input (a missing or wrong option, a bad record id, an unknown session), tier (an unknown tier, or a tier with no model for the agent) and budget (a Console budget or Console config refusal).
D4. Failure causes: lane_create (basicly worktree create failed, and nothing was sent to the agent), agent_exit (the agent exited non-zero) and no_answer (the agent exited 0 but printed no answer or no session id).
D5. Blocked state. The tracker keeps one blocked status (KNOWN_STATUSES, src/basicly/loop_state.py). A dispatch outcome other than answered gives a record its cause code: the outcome and the cause above, for example "usage_limit/reset_known" or "failed/agent_exit". A reader decides from the code, not from prose: wait for the reset after usage_limit, fix the input after refused, and repair or retry after failed.
D6. The vocabulary is data in one place (orch_relay), and orch delegate, the saved failure file and the README read it from there. An outcome or cause outside the list is refused by a test.
Implementation: the next child of basicly-qpr2xmr.4, "orch delegate ends with one outcome and a cause code".

## Context
MEASURED (gh run view, last 10 compatibility runs, 2026-11-27 11:18-11:57 UTC):

- The wheel smoke (.scripts/compatibility_smoke.py) runs three independent scenarios one after another, each in its own temp repo: upgrade from v0.27.0 about 24 s, exercise no-comments about 64 s, exercise no-comment-ratchet about 64 s (log timestamps 11:48:18, 11:48:42, 11:49:46, end about 11:50:50). Each git commit through the consumer hooks takes 6-16 s on Windows.
PROPOSAL (largest saving first; none removes a check):
1. Run the three smoke scenarios in parallel inside the script (threads or processes; each has its own temp repo and venv). Expected Windows smoke about 65 s instead of 103-154 s, saving about 60-90 s. Script edit only (.scripts/), not a workflow edit; ordinary work. Fails if the scenarios share the runtime venv: they do (one runtime/Scripts/basicly.exe), which is read-only use, but uv pip install of the baseline in the upgrade scenario writes to it, so the upgrade scenario needs its own venv. 2. pytest -n 4 for the focused regressions on Windows (pytest-xdist is already in the dev group). Expected 82 s to about 30-40 s (assumed: 4 vCPU on windows-latest, not measured). 3. Split the Windows job into two matrix entries, regressions and smoke, in parallel. Critical path about 45 s setup + max(regressions, smoke). Workflow edit; costs one more Windows runner per run. Only needed if 1 and 2 do not bring the job under about 180 s.
4. Shallow checkout (fetch-depth 1) instead of full history saves an estimated 15-25 s of the 25-35 s checkout. Not established: whether the focused tests or the smoke need history or tags. Needs a probe before any edit.
Not proposed: moving a check to nightly. With 1 and 2 the job is about 32+20+35+65, roughly 150 s, so no removal or move is needed; no council.
Recommended: approve 1 as ordinary work in a lane of mine after my two lanes land (it is a built item, so WIP), and decide 2 with a probe run first.

payload.text:
[terminal probe, relayed by basicly-meta 2026-11-27] Run: python3 -I probe_snapshot.py <empty dir> <repo><redacted:posix-absolute-path> staged-snapshot.py. On 0.49.6 it prints "publish raised FileNotFoundError ... tree/b/gone.md", "index: M pin", "worktree gone.md exists: True keep: k". Expected after the fix: "publish ok", the index shows D b/gone.md and M b/keep.md, gone.md is removed from the checkout and keep.md reads k2. The regression test turns this into a pytest case in the existing staged-snapshot tests.

import sys, subprocess, tempfile, shutil
from pathlib import Path
repo = Path(sys.argv[1]); hooks = Path(sys.argv[2])
sys.path.insert(0, str(hooks))
import importlib.util
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("snap", hooks / sys.argv[3]); snap = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); sys.modules["snap"] = snap; spec.loader.exec_module(snap)
def g(*a, cwd=repo, env=None): return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=cwd, env=env, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
g("init", "-q"); g("config", "user.email", "x@example.invalid"); g("config", "user.name", "x")
(repo/"b").mkdir(); (repo/"b"/"keep.md").write_text("k\n"); (repo/"b"/"gone.md").write_text("g\n"); (repo/"pin").write_text("1\n")
g("add", "-A"); g("commit", "-qm", "init")
(repo/"pin").write_text("2\n"); g("add", "pin")
d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
state = snap.prepare(repo, d)
env = {**__import__("os").environ, **snap.job_env(state, "pre-commit")}
(state.tree/"b"/"gone.md").unlink(); (state.tree/"b"/"keep.md").write_text("k2\n")
g("add", "-A", "--", "b", cwd=state.tree, env=env)
try:
    snap.publish(state); print("publish ok")
except Exception as e:
    print("publish raised", type(e).__name__, e)
print("index:", g("diff", "--cached", "--name-status").strip().replace("\n", " | "))
print("worktree gone.md exists:", (repo/"b"/"gone.md").exists(), "keep:", (repo/"b"/"keep.md").read_text().strip())

payload.text:
[design 2026-11-27 basicly-ux, read-only] Delete a lane's merged retry and PR branches in basicly worktree cleanup.
NOW: worktree.cleanup -> remote_branches.reclaim -> delete_landed(main, harness/<lane>) deletes only the recorded lane branch. Its guard: ls-remote reads the head; the head must be on origin/<base> by first-parent trunk, ancestry or git cherry (every commit "-"), or unlanded() finds no changed path missing; then ONE push "git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/B:<head> origin :refs/heads/B"; it prints "deleted origin/B: ..." or returns "kept origin/B: <reason>". Retry branches harness/<lane>-N and PR branches pr/<lane>/<head12> (delivery_pr._push) are never looked at.
DENY RULE: Bash(git *push*--delete*), "git *push* :**" and shell(git push --delete) match commands an agent types. The engine's own subprocess is not an agent Bash call, so the design changes no permission rule. Agents keep running only "basicly worktree cleanup <name>".
DESIGN
1. Candidates: one "git ls-remote --heads origin" for refs/heads/harness/<lane>-* and refs/heads/pr/<lane>/*. Keep only names that fully match ^harness/<lane>-[0-9]+$ or ^pr/<lane>/[0-9a-f]{12}$.
2. Collision guard: skip and name a candidate that is the recorded branch of another session file or a registered worktree. Lane "foo" must never delete lane "foo-2"'s own branch harness/foo-2.
3. Proof: the base is the record's base, else origin's default branch (git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD). A candidate is deleted only if its head is an ancestor of origin/<base>, or every commit is patch-equivalent by git cherry. The path-only fallback (unlanded) is NOT used for candidates: a retry branch must prove its head, as the owner's approval says.
4. One guarded step per branch: one push per ref, each with --force-with-lease on the head that step 1 read, no batch refspec. A changed head makes the lease refuse, and the branch is kept.
5. Output: one line per candidate, "deleted origin/B: head <sha12> is on origin/<base> (ancestor|patch-equivalent)" or "kept origin/B: <reason>". The summary line counts deleted and kept.
6. This runs after the lane-branch step, also when that branch was kept, and also with missing_ok (the landing tool's cleanup after a merge).
ACCEPTANCE (EARS)
- WHEN cleanup runs for lane L, THE ENGINE SHALL delete each origin/harness/L-N and origin/pr/L/<12hex> whose head is an ancestor of, or patch-equivalent to, origin's default branch, one guarded push per branch, and print each deleted name with its head.
- IF a candidate's head is not proved on the default branch, THEN THE ENGINE SHALL keep it and print its name and the reason.
- IF a candidate is the recorded branch of another session or worktree, THEN THE ENGINE SHALL keep it and name that owner.
- IF ls-remote fails, or the head or base is not fetched, THEN THE ENGINE SHALL keep every candidate and print the command to run.
- IF the remote head changes between the read and the push, THEN the lease refuses and THE ENGINE SHALL keep the branch.
- A test reproduces the leftover retry branch first (record criterion): a bare origin holding harness/L, harness/L-2 (landed) and harness/L-3 (unlanded); cleanup deletes L-2, keeps L-3 and prints both.
HOW IT FAILS
- A retry branch that carries a fixup squashed into a different commit on main is not patch-equivalent, so it is kept. That is safe, but the owner still deletes it by hand. A follow-up could allow the path check behind a flag.
- A lane name containing regex characters: the name must be escaped before matching (test it).
- GitHub's "delete head branch on merge" may delete pr/L/* first; then ls-remote finds none, which is a no-op.
- A classifier may still flag the engine's push if a hook inspects subprocess argv. Untested; the existing lane-branch delete has run in landings today without a refusal (basicly's cleanups of vec4m5f and qag8oms).
- Network: one ls-remote plus one push per branch; for a lane with 5 retries that is 6 network calls.

IF a candidate's head is not proved on the default branch, THEN THE ENGINE SHALL keep it and print its name, the reason, and the exact command a person would run to land or delete it.
IF a candidate is the recorded branch of another session or registered worktree, THEN THE ENGINE SHALL keep it and name that owner.
IF git ls-remote fails, or the head or the base is not fetched, THEN THE ENGINE SHALL keep every candidate and print the command to run first.
IF the remote head changes between the read and the push, THEN the lease refuses and THE ENGINE SHALL keep the branch and print why.
